decision_points.question: Should --no-chrome be hard-coded into every test/runtime path?
decision_points.decision: Keep tests neutral by adding ClaudeCodeRuntime::with_interactive_args, and inject --no-chrome only in the production bridge runtime unless AGENT_BRIDGE_CLAUDE_INTERACTIVE_NO_CHROME is falsey.
decision_points.reason: This preserves testability with /bin/cat and keeps the behavior operator-overridable.

decision_points.question: Should the result be trusted before MCP reconnect?
decision_points.decision: No. Treat the install as stale until reconnect verifies the live MCP servers execute the new agent-bridge.real.
decision_points.reason: The MCP process can keep an older binary alive after installation.

outcome.behavior_change: Production Claude Code interactive sessions receive --no-chrome by default, avoiding the first-run browser prompt that blocked send_input dogfooding.
evidence: installed agent-bridge.real verified by hash and BuildID
direct MCP smoke with /bin/cat delivered two follow-up inputs
post-reconnect doctor reported ok=true, fails=0, warns=0
known_limits: The direct smoke used /bin/cat for deterministic input echo rather than a full live Claude Code conversation.
Operator can disable the production --no-chrome default with AGENT_BRIDGE_CLAUDE_INTERACTIVE_NO_CHROME=0|false|no|off.

reflection.lesson: Interactive-agent fixes need both runtime dogfood and post-reconnect binary verification; otherwise a correct patch can appear broken because the live MCP process still runs an older binary or the child process is blocked on a first-run prompt.
reusable_workflow: dogfood with a minimal deterministic child when possible
make runtime defaults explicit and operator-overridable
run focused tests plus all-target check
reflection.falsifier: If future live Claude Code sessions still stall before accepting input with default settings, this experience should be marked incomplete and a new fixture should capture the actual prompt/output blocker.

promotion.suggested_trigger: When changing interactive agent runtimes, send_input semantics, or MCP-installed binaries.
